messages:
alex: Quick proposal — run a head-to-head runtime benchmark that forces identical external factors: same prompt files, identical decoding params, identical stop sequences, and explicit tokenizer alignment. We keep kernel and batching choices controlled so we can isolate perf deltas from model diffs.

maya: +1. Can you drop the exact harness commands and the config we'll pin? want to run locally then on dedicated infra.

alex: Sure. Two modes: replay harness (deterministic) and synthetic poisson load. Replay is for apples-to-apples answer quality + latency; synthetic for stress/concurrency. Example replay command:

```
./replay_harness --input prompts/benchmark_set.jsonl --model A --model B \
  --decode.sampling=false --decode.temperature=0 --stop-sequences='["\n\n"]' \
  --tokenizer=hf/llama-tokenizer --seed=42 --kv.warmup_passes=2 \
  --pin-kernels={"matmul":"fp16"} --batching.max_batch=4 --concurrency=8
```

alex: Notes: --decode.sampling=false + temperature=0 to ensure deterministic decoding; stop sequences must be applied post-tokenizer with identical rules; tokenizer must be the same HF file (or a byte-for-byte mapped tokenizer). KV warmup of 2 full sequences to populate cache similarly across models.

trent: Kernel selection caveat — some models have custom fused kernels (eg attention rotary optimizations). For fair comparison we either: a) force fallback kernels to a common ABI, or b) explicitly list kernel variants in the benchmark metadata and report them. I vote (b) and record kernel map so we can attribute speedups.

sam: Batching heuristics: don't let autotuner change batch shape between experiments. Set fixed max_batch=4 and a fixed micro-batch policy. Also measure tail latency at p95/p99 and effective throughput with identical queuing. If we need to show production impact, run with real inter-arrival times (replay) + synthetic poisson at the same mean rate.

maya: On tokenizer alignment: I added a tiny script to assert token boundaries and stop-seq equivalence before running. Example:

```
# check_token_alignment.py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
A = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizers/hfA.json')
B = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizers/hfB.json')
for s in open('prompts/benchmark_set.jsonl'):
  src = s.strip()
  if A.encode(src).ids != B.encode(src).ids:
    print('MISMATCH', src)
    break
else:
  print('TOKENIZERS MATCH')
```

maya: We should fail fast if tokenizers don't match. That invalidates any apples-to-apples claim.

perf-bot: perf-bot: Preliminary run on dev cluster (small) — p50/p95/p99 for model A: 20/62/180 ms; model B: 24/78/210 ms. kernel_map: {matmul:fp16, attention:optimized_rotary}. Replay run used --concurrency=4 and --batching.max_batch=2. See /perf/artifacts/1793456789 for raw traces.

alex: Good. Please attach raw traces and the kernel_map JSON to the spreadsheet. Also capture KV cache metrics: bytes written/read, hit rate by layer, and whether we had cache thrashing when sequence length varied.

trent: KV observation: model B's implementation evicts earlier because its KV tiled layout causes more L2 misses on our GPUs. We should capture hardware counters (L2 hit/miss) during run. If eviction explains p99 spikes, that's a real runtime regression, not a model perf gap.

sam: Perf regression checklist for these runs:
- deterministic seeds and decode params
- tokenizer alignment check pass
- kernel map included
- batching/concurrency pinned
- KV warmup and metrics recorded
- hardware counters collected
- traffic mode (replay vs synthetic) recorded

alex: CI integration: add a minimal harness job that runs the tokenization check + a single short replay (10 prompts) on PRs changing kernels or runtime. If it regresses, attach a perf-bot summary.

ci-bot: ci-bot: created job runtime/regress/quick-lexical-check — runs on PRs touching eng-runtime/*kernels* and eng-runtime/*batching*; posts perf summary as comment. (job id: rtqc-1793456789) :robot_face:

maya: Plan: I'll run a full head-to-head on dedicated infra tonight with the pinned config and upload traces. Alex, can you add the kernel_map exporter to the harness so we record exact symbol names?

alex: Yep, will push a small change to record kernel symbols + nvperf counters. Also will include a flag --force-fallback-kernels for the fallback ABIs if we need a strict baseline.

sam: When you post results, please include a short table: model, p50/p95/p99, throughput @ target latency, kernel_map, tokenizer_hash, kv_hit_rate. That's what SRE/product will look at.

maya: OK starting run now, will ping when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
